heading: SEBI Proposal: FPIs in Physically Settled Commodity Trades
tldr: SEBI is considering allowing Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) to participate in physically settled commodity derivative contracts.
This initiative aims to remove a significant tax hurdle that has previously deterred FPIs from this segment.
FPIs have largely avoided these contracts due to ambiguities surrounding the tax treatment of physical delivery.
Opening up this market could enhance liquidity and price discovery in India's commodity exchanges, particularly for bullion and base metals.
The move is expected to attract more foreign capital and deepen India's financial markets.
caption:
Ever wondered why foreign investors don't trade much in Indian gold or metals? A big reason was unclear tax rules for physical delivery. Now, India's market regulator, SEBI, is looking to fix this! This could bring more foreign money into our commodity markets, making them stronger and more active. This is great news for India's growing economy. Read more about it here!
